setup.title: Setup
setup.readyBody: All {{count}} steps are in order. Daily work happens in Agents and in Automations.
setup.firstBody: Nothing has been checked yet. Review each step or verify them all at once; it takes a couple of minutes.

engines.title: Engines authenticated
engines.never: No engine has been checked yet
engines.none: No engines are configured in Agents.
engines.err_subscription: {{label}}: there is no active session on the server.
engines.help: To fix it, run this in the server’s terminal:

dagu.title: Agents connected to workflows
dagu.down: The agents' connection to workflows is not answering.
dagu.never: Checked after the agents are applied

extension.failed: The extension's check failed. Review its configuration: if the keys changed or are examples, enter new ones.

bots.title: Agents
bots.subtitle: They are defined here and applied to Agents. Fine-tuning happens there, afterwards.
bots.bannerBody: Agents keeps using the previous version until you apply them.
bots.draftConflict: The project configuration changed. Your draft is saved. Review it or discard it before applying new changes.
bots.discardBody: The panel goes back to the project’s team.yaml. Agents does not change.
bots.emptyBody: Create the first one here. Then apply it and it becomes available in Agents.
bots.enginesUnknown: The engines have not been checked yet.
bots.architectHint: To create, inspect, update or delete agents, open Agents and choose Bot Architect. The manual form remains available.
bots.runtimeHint: Live roster, including the chief. Changes in Agents appear automatically every 5 seconds.
bots.runtimeError: The Agents roster could not be refreshed. The previous roster may be out of date.
bots.runtimeEmpty: There are no agents in Agents.
bots.importDraftHint: Apply or discard the draft before importing another agent.
bots.versionUnavailable: Git status could not be verified. Import is disabled.
bots.versionHint: “In project” and “In snapshot” indicate a definition saved in the latest commit; later native edits may not be saved.
bots.importDirtyHint: Project configuration has uncommitted changes. Commit or discard them before importing.

team.name: Department name
team.briefHint: Every agent in the department gets them in its prompt. They apply when you review and apply the changes.
team.createHint: Agents creates it empty on apply. Then move agents with each one's Department field. Renaming and deleting are managed in Agents.
team.nameTaken: A department with that name already exists.
team.briefLong: The shared instructions exceed the 24,000 bytes Agents accepts.

templates.title: Add a department
templates.body: Ready-made departments from the installed extensions: their agents, shared instructions, skills and group chats. Choosing one saves its skills in the project and opens the change as a draft for you to review and apply.
templates.draftHint: Apply or discard the pending changes before adding a department.
templates.replaces: This department already exists: the draft replaces its agents and group chats.

form.name: Name
form.engineHint: Only the engines configured in the project are shown.
form.enginesUnchecked: The engines have not been checked yet: these are the ones team.yaml already uses.
form.soulFilePlaceholder: Leave it empty to keep using the file. If you write here, these instructions replace it.
form.skillsReadOnly: Listed for reference: for now they are edited in team.yaml.
form.workflowsHint: It can query the project’s workflows from Agents.
form.workflowsLocked: It can query the project’s workflows. To remove it, change its cwd in team.yaml.
form.deleteBody: The bot is marked for removal. Applying the changes permanently deletes the bot and its conversation history in Agents.
form.saveNote: Saving does not apply: it stays pending until “Review and apply”.
form.errNameDup: A agent with that name already exists. Choose another one.
form.errSoulLong: The text is too long: {{extra}} bytes over. Move long data to a file and reference it.
form.notFound: That agent is not in team.yaml.
form.skillsExt: They come from the installed extensions and from confirmed third-party skills. They are applied with the agent’s other changes.
form.skillsNeedRoot: They need the project’s tools: turn on “Uses workflows” to use them.
form.piHumanRequestContext: To resume requests in this conversation, Pi can read this agent's conversations and those it opened with other agents.
form.piHumanRequestBlocked: Conversation listing is blocked. Pi can create requests, but cannot receive questions or return to this conversation until it is enabled.
form.teamHint: Optional. Choose a department or type a new one. After moving an agent, save its application permissions again for the new department.
form.teamLeave: Choose a department: Agents does not move the agent to General when this field is empty.
form.teamChief: This agent is its department's chief of staff and can manage the department's agents.

preview.deleteHistoryWarning: Deleting a bot from Agents permanently removes its conversation history. The configuration snapshot does not contain that history.
preview.title: Preview of changes
preview.emptyBody: What the panel has already matches Agents.
preview.snapshotNote: Before applying, the tuning done in Agents is saved to git.
preview.doneTitle: Applied. You can use them in Agents now.

apps.title: Apps
apps.subtitle: Everything that runs in the project. Framework apps open here; the rest, in a new tab.
apps.downDetail: Not responding at the last check.
apps.emptyTitle: This project has no apps of its own yet.
apps.emptyHint: Copy the template to create the first one:

healthTip.down: Not responding at the last check · {{host}}

observ.title: AI usage
observ.subtitle: How much the project's agents use AI: tokens, cost and your subscription usage.
observ.mock: This view requires the real stack; no invented consumption is displayed.
observ.loadError: The summary could not be loaded. Refresh it and, if it fails, check the log in Automations.
observ.partial: Partial coverage. Missing sources do not mean zero usage.
observ.costNote: USD reported by the engine, not reconciled with invoices. The subscription equivalent is an estimate at list price: it is not your bill or your quota, and it excludes the fixed fee.
observ.coverage: {{count}} turns or attempts without an amount
observ.noAlerts: No thresholds exceeded in available data.
observ.alertNote: Local advisories; no agents are stopped and no messages are sent. Settings: project/observability.json. Monetary thresholds use reported API cost only and may have incomplete coverage. The subscription threshold (subscriptionPercent) warns about the account, not the project.
observ.usage: Usage by agent, model and engine
observ.conversationModel: Conversations group delegations across models and engines; they are filtered by agent and period only.

warning.invalidLedgerRows: Some usage records could not be read.
warning.invalidArtifacts: Some artifacts could not be read.
warning.runDetailsUnavailable: Some run details could not be read.
warning.invalidPricing: The price table has invalid entries; they were ignored.

alert.longRun: Run active for {{value}} s · threshold {{limit}} s
alert.longConversation: Conversation active for {{value}} s · threshold {{limit}} s

observ.tokenNote: New input + cached input = total input. Reasoning is included in output.

plan.title: Your subscription usage
plan.note: Based on your subscription usage as reported by the provider. It belongs to the account, not the project: it includes what you use from other projects, other computers and the provider's own app.
plan.unavailable: No subscription data right now. Agents keep working; it is checked again on the next refresh.
plan.none: No agent uses a subscription engine, or the provider does not report usage.
plan.unknownNote: "Unknown" is normal: some plans lack one of the windows, or the provider did not answer.

observ.pricing: Amounts the engine does not report (for example Codex) are estimated with the list-price table of {{date}}: an estimated equivalent, not your bill or a share of your subscription. A model not in the table shows as "{{unknown}}".
observ.pricingProject: Includes this project's own prices from project/pricing.json.

ext.title: Installed extensions
ext.manage: Removing an extension is a terminal task. To upgrade all of them:
ext.emptyHint: Install one from the marketplace or from its repo:
ext.skillsTip: Skills: enable them on a agent

setup.keep: Set. Leave empty to keep it
setup.private: Values are stored encrypted and never shown again.
setup.checkFailed: Saved, but the extension's check failed. Review the values.
setup.stillMissing: Saved, but required values are still missing.
setup.invalidInput: Review the values: no line breaks and at most 4096 characters.

setup.busy: Another configuration is being saved. Try again in a few seconds.
setup.saveFailed: Could not save. Nothing was changed.
setup.unavailable: The setup service is unavailable. Restart the project.
setup.stepOpen: Open the keys page and create a new key
setup.nothingDetected: No key recognized. Paste the whole block the page shows, or enter the values one by one.
setup.oneByOne: Enter the values one by one
setup.example: That looks like an example, not your key ({{names}}). Create a new key on the keys page and copy the block shown in the key's dialog: it is shown in full only once.

ext.importHint: Start imports from Knowledge after uploading and selecting documents.

skills.emptyHint: Find one below, read it, then install it.
skills.searchLabel: Search skills by text or paste a repository
skills.searchHint: Searches the project’s repositories and the public directory skills.sh. You can also paste a repository (owner/repo) or a GitHub or skills.sh address.
skills.untrusted: third-party text: read it before you accept it
skills.extraFiles_one: {{count}} more file (kept in the project; the agent only receives SKILL.md)
skills.extraFiles_other: {{count}} more files (kept in the project; the agent only receives SKILL.md)
skills.added: {{name}} is installed and off for every agent. Review it under “Installed third-party skills” to be able to switch it on.
skills.scanMissing: Agents has not scanned it yet. It cannot be confirmed without that scan.
skills.scanClean: The Agents scan found no warnings
skills.modified: Installed content changed. Update it to review it again.
skills.iRead: I read the skill and know where it comes from
skills.confirmed: {{name}} is confirmed. Switch it on in each agent that should use it.
skills.updateTip: Preview the latest source revision before installing it.
skills.updated: Updated to {{commit}}. Review it again, then review and apply the agents to synchronize their skills.
skills.removeBlocked: Switch it off first in the agents that use it
skills.terminalNote: Remove: mise run skills:remove <name>. Sources are chosen in project/skill-sources.yaml.

stateTip.modified: The file is no longer what was installed; no agent gets it
stateTip.scan: The Agents scan is missing; no agent gets it
stateTip.review: A person still has to read and confirm it; no agent gets it
stateTip.ready: It can be switched on per agent, in the agent’s profile

originTip.directory: Named by the public directory skills.sh; the files are read from its git repository

market.title: Marketplace
market.never: Read the catalogs in project/marketplaces.yaml to see the available extensions.
market.githubAccess: This project's host cannot access the GitHub repository. Check its account or configure a read credential with access to that repository.
market.done: {{id}} {{version}} is installed and committed ({{commit}}). If it needs keys, set them on its card, under Installed.
market.hint: Installing commits only the extension's files; upgrading works on a clean copy of the last commit. Neither touches your uncommitted changes, and both load processes and routes without a restart. From the terminal too:
market.removeHint: Its files, processes, routes and workflows are removed in one commit. Its data in .data/ext and its saved keys are kept. Switch off its skills in your agents first.

extensionPage.missing: This extension page is not installed.

connections.title: Connectors for your agents
connections.description: Open Agents, go to Apps and connect a service or add an MCP server. Authorize your account there.
connections.failed: Could not read connections. Try again.
connections.empty: No MCP servers are configured yet.
connections.nativeOnly: Only in Agents: recreate after restore
connections.assignment: Then ask Bot Architect to assign the tools each agent needs. Enabled does not mean tested; verify a read operation. Connected-app accounts and permissions are managed in Access settings, in Agents.

connectors.title: Connectors
connectors.subtitle: Connect your apps and choose which agents can use them.
connectors.mcpHint: Add a remote server or a local command. Agents tests connections and holds credentials.
connectors.setupRequired: Use Set up Composio above to enable these apps.
connectors.partialCatalog: The catalog is incomplete. Refresh to query the services again.
connectors.partialAccounts: The complete account inventory could not be verified.
connectors.name: Server name
connectors.secretHint: The credential goes directly to Agents. It is never displayed after saving or sent to automation logs.
connectors.noMcp: No MCP servers have been added yet.
connectors.nativePersistence: Definitions created here are versioned. Reauthorize OAuth accounts after a clean restore.
connectors.projectServersHint: Their definitions are managed in project files or extensions. You can also assign them to agents here.
connectors.signInRequired: This server needs sign-in. Choose Authorize account.
connectors.testFailed: The test did not pass. Check the connection and try again.
connectors.createdSignIn: Server saved. Complete authorization to enable it.
connectors.createdOff: Server saved and disabled: the test did not pass.
connectors.requestFailed: The operation could not be completed. Check the connection and try again.
connectors.invalidName: Use up to 32 lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens or underscores, starting with a letter.
connectors.invalidUrl: Enter an HTTP or HTTPS URL without credentials. Put secrets in the header.
connectors.invalidHeader: Check the header name and use a single-line credential.
connectors.aliasRequired: Enter a name to distinguish the new account from the existing one.
connectors.authorizationHint: Complete authorization in the provider window, then check the result here.
connectors.callback: Return URL · only if the provider requires it
connectors.authorizationFailed: Authorization did not complete. Start it again.
connectors.botAccessHint: Select the MCP servers this agent may use. Each selection enables all their tools; app account permissions remain in Agents. The preview preserves other servers and native tools.
connectors.accessSaved: Permissions saved and verified in Agents.
connectors.botFailed: Could not read or change the agent. Check the Bot Architect run in Automations.
connectors.removeHint: This connection will be removed from Agents. Agent selections are not broadened or changed automatically.

failed.apps: Could not read the app catalog.
failed.accounts: Could not read accounts. Previous data is hidden.

connectors.nativeBlocked: Restricted by the access set in Agents
connectors.directHint: These services use their own MCP and authorization. Composio is not required.

direct.whop: Connect your Whop account through its official MCP. It includes commerce and payment tools; assign access to the appropriate agents.
direct.agentcard: Connect your Agentcard account through its official MCP. Purchase approvals and operations remain with the provider.

connectors.claudeHint: Native options for this project’s Claude agents. They apply to subsequent tasks. Personal configuration and skills remain local to this computer.
connectors.claudeUserMcp: Also use my Claude Code MCP servers
connectors.claudeUserMcpHint: Adds MCP servers and connectors from your Claude Code configuration to the project’s servers. More tools use more tokens per message.
connectors.claudeUserSkills: Also use my Claude Code skills
connectors.claudeUserSkillsHint: Loads ~/.claude/skills with scripts and reference files. Edits arrive directly; this option does not add hooks, MCP servers or CLAUDE.md.
connectors.preferencesFailed: Could not read or save these options. Check the preferences workflow in Automations.

botConnectors.title: Connectors
botConnectors.hint: Choose the MCP servers this agent may use. Enabling a server allows all its tools. Existing partial access is shown and preserved until you change it.
botConnectors.draftHint: MCP changes: Save → Review and apply.
botConnectors.failed: Could not verify the connector inventory. Refresh before changing permissions.
botConnectors.claudeSources: Claude Code sources for this engine: MCP {{mcp}} · skills {{skills}}. Configure them in the Connectors tab.
botConnectors.codexSources: This agent uses Codex. Claude Code switches do not apply to this engine. Personal engine MCP servers are not listed in this project inventory.
botConnectors.otherSources: Personal sources depend on the chosen engine. Manage connections and authorization in the Connectors tab.
botConnectors.pendingDraft: The agent list has pending changes. Review and apply or discard them before changing permissions from this screen.
botConnectors.appsHint: Accounts authorized through Composio in this project.
botConnectors.appsFailed: Could not read connected applications. Try refreshing.
botConnectors.appPermissionsHint: Application permissions are saved separately from the agent form. Existing tool restrictions are preserved. The first change creates an explicit app list; newly connected apps require permission.
botConnectors.saveBotFirst: Save and apply this agent first to configure its application permissions.
botConnectors.permissionsFailed: Could not read or save app permissions. Refresh and preview again. No success is confirmed until native verification passes.
botConnectors.appChangeHint: Review before applying. This does not change your account authorization.
botConnectors.reviewAppPermissions: Apply these application permissions to this agent?

composioSetup.title: Composio
composioSetup.hint: Set up your project once, then connect your apps from this panel.
composioSetup.connectedHint: Composio is configured. Choose an app and authorize your account.
composioSetup.keyLocation: If prompted, choose Platform and select your project. Then open Settings → API Keys and copy the key.
composioSetup.paste: Paste the key in the field below and select Save and verify.
composioSetup.authorize: Once saved, select Choose an app. Start Gmail, Slack or another app authorization from Fyso.
composioSetup.private: The key is encrypted in the project. It is never displayed or sent through agent history.
composioSetup.ready: Composio is ready. Choose an app to connect your account.
composioSetup.activationPending: The key is saved and encrypted, but Agents could not activate it. Try saving it again.
composioSetup.invalidInput: Enter a valid Composio project key.
composioSetup.invalidKey: Composio rejected the key. Copy a project key with access to Auth Configs.
composioSetup.providerUnavailable: Could not verify Composio. Try again shortly.
composioSetup.pendingSecrets: Project secrets have pending changes. Save them before setting up Composio.
composioSetup.busy: Another configuration is being saved. Please wait.
composioSetup.saveFailed: Could not save the configuration. Please try again.

connectionFlow.title: Connect {{app}}
connectionFlow.preparing: Preparing the {{app}} authorization link. Stay in this window.
connectionFlow.failed: Could not complete the {{app}} connection. Return to the catalog and try connecting again.
connectionFlow.openHint: The button opens a new tab. Keep this Fyso tab open to continue.
connectionFlow.approveHint: In the new tab, sign in to your {{app}} account and approve the permissions you want to grant.
connectionFlow.returnHint: When finished, come back here. We will check the connection automatically.
connectionFlow.waiting: Waiting for you to authorize {{app}}. Return to this tab when finished.
connectionFlow.callbackPending: When finished, paste the return address shown by the provider here.
connectionFlow.complete: {{app}} authorization is confirmed. Return to the catalog to see the connection.
connectionFlow.checkFailed: Could not check the connection yet. Select I authorized my account · check to retry.

access.partial: Partial access: kept until you change it

detail.saveTipApps: Application accesses apply on save; everything else stays pending until “Review and apply”.

mcp.title: Run the project from your AI
mcp.intro: Connect Claude or Codex to this project's MCP to create agents, install extensions and check its status by chatting.
mcp.serverTip: MCP server name in your app
mcp.hostNote: It is configured on the machine that runs the project, for its user.
mcp.demo: Demo mode: actions are simulated and change no app.

stateTip.on: The server is in its configuration
stateTip.off: Installed on this machine, without the server yet

openTip.claude-desktop: Restarts Claude Desktop and opens a chat with the test message
openTip.codex: Opens a new thread in the project folder with the test message

after.claude-desktop: Restart Claude Desktop to load it, or use Open a conversation.

mcp.missingHint: Install it and come back to this page
mcp.disconnectTip: Disconnect · the project and its agents stay as they are
mcp.statusError: Could not read the apps' status.
mcp.remoteTitle: You opened the panel from another machine
mcp.remoteBody: Connecting from here would configure the server's apps, not yours. To connect your agent from another machine the project needs HTTPS: install an HTTPS access extension on it (for example, NetBird).
mcp.remoteReadyTitle: Connect your agent to this project
mcp.remoteReadyBody: Press Run to see here the command ready for each client (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI or another). You can also run this command in a terminal on the project's machine.
mcp.tryTitle: Try the connection in a new conversation
mcp.prompt: Read fyso_context and run fyso_status to review my project. Tell me what I have and what to set up first.
mcp.troubleTitle: If it does not show up
mcp.trouble1: Check that the app and the project tools are installed for the user that runs the project.
mcp.trouble2: Connect again and open a new conversation.
mcp.trouble3: Check the error and the log of the fyso-agent-connect workflow in Automations.
mcp.setupTitle: Run the project from your AI
mcp.setupBody: Optional: connect Claude or Codex to configure the project by chatting.
mcp.remoteSecret: These commands include this project's token and OAuth secret: whoever has them can use its tools (with OAuth, they also need a panel user). Copy them only on your own machine.

remoteNote.env: The token stays in an environment variable; add the export to your shell profile.
remoteNote.json: Configuration for clients that use a JSON file.
remoteNote.oauth: Add a custom connector with the URL. ChatGPT and claude.ai register themselves; if they ask for a Client ID and Client Secret, use these. When connecting, sign in with your panel user.
remoteNote.oauthCli: Then run /mcp in Claude Code and sign in with your panel user. The callback uses local port 33418.
remoteNote.oauthHub: Settings › Connectors › Add custom connector: paste the URL and, under Advanced settings, the Client ID and the Client Secret the shared login's administrator gives you. When connecting, sign in with your user.

remoteError.httpsRequired: The project has no HTTPS access yet.
remoteError.noToken: The token is not available. Press Run again.
remoteError.origin: Open the panel from its usual address and try again.
remoteError.unauthorized: Your session expired. Sign in again.
remoteError.failed: The connection commands could not be fetched.

update.title: Framework
update.refTip: Template tag, branch or commit; empty: the latest tag
update.srcPlaceholder: Path of a local clone, when this host cannot read the repository
update.done: Updated {{from}} → {{to}} (commit {{commit}}). If the project's services changed, restart the project.

identity.title: Project identity
identity.body: name, colour and icon in every app
identity.name: Name
identity.nameHint: Shown by the panel, the login, Automations and Agent chat.
identity.accentInvalid: The colour must be a hex value such as #6e1fff.
identity.iconHint: PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG. Saved square, up to 256 px.
identity.iconInvalid: That image could not be read. Try a PNG or a JPG.
identity.restartNote: The panel, the icons and the login background change on save. The name on the login, Automations and Agent chat changes when the project restarts. Typography and corners apply to the panel.
identity.backgroundHint: A photo or large image. Saved as JPEG, up to 1600 px.
identity.backgroundInvalid: That image could not be used. Try a JPG or a PNG.
